owned_invariants: The task has a nonempty training list whose points carry an exact integer id, a number of proposers from 1 to 64, and optionally the coefficients of a baseline polynomial (default: the zero polynomial). The sealed part has the held-out points, each with an integer id and exact rational x and y.
A run in which a training id is also a held-out id is refused as SPLIT_OVERLAP, with the shared ids, before any proposer is asked.

Every proposer is asked under its own stage, proposer:K, with the same prompt. A proposer's score is the number of held-out points its polynomial hits exactly; a reply whose coefficients cannot be read scores -1, and a proposer that gave no reply has no score.

The winner is the highest score, and on a tie the stage name that sorts first as text. The run is certified as WINNER_SELECTED only when the winner's score is strictly above the baseline polynomial's score on the same points.
When no proposer replied the run is refused as NO_ADMISSIBLE_REPLY.
The verdict's detail names the winner, every score, the baseline score and the number of held-out points. It carries no held-out value.
boundaries: The held-out points reach the host in the sealed part and never appear in a prompt; the sealed-value guard of families.rs checks each prompt.
Scores count exact hits. A polynomial that is close but not equal at a point scores nothing there.
Stage names sort as text, so proposer:10 sorts before proposer:2. The tie rule is stated in those terms.
Beating the baseline on the held-out points of one task is not evidence about other tasks.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.
